status: unrefereed research candidate; internal AI-assisted review only

target.citation: Hwang, Ting & Zakamska (2022), MNRAS 512, 3383-3399, Appendix B (uniqueness of the eccentricity-to-angle mapping)

model: Conditional on eccentricity e in [0,1): mean anomaly uniform on [0,2pi); orbital frame Haar-distributed on SO(3), independent of phase; Gamma in [0,pi] is the angle between the error-free sky projections of relative position and relative velocity. Observations i.i.d. from one population.

claims.statement: For 0<e<1 and 0<gamma<pi, p(gamma|e) = [acosh(1/e) - 1{|cos gamma|>e} acosh(|cos gamma|/e)] / (pi sin^2 gamma); the circular case is -log|cos gamma| / (pi sin^2 gamma).
Mixtures of the likelihood over any Borel probability law F on [0,1) are classical Abel transforms; the angle law determines F, including atoms, by an explicit inverse.
Closed angle laws for power-law eccentricity populations f(e) = (alpha+1) e^alpha; the thermal law alpha = 1 is the unique law giving uniform angles.
Every circularity moment E (1-e^2)^(s/2) is the mean of an explicit angle observable; e.g. E sqrt(1-e^2) = (pi/2) E sin^3 Gamma. Estimator claims hold for s >= 0 or when the moment is finite.
An eccentricity functional has at most one symmetric integrable unbiased single-angle observable (almost everywhere).
E e^2 = 1/2 + E cos 2Gamma - (1/2) E cos 4Gamma, and E e^4 is likewise a finite Fourier sum.
One-line estimators of power-law indices with Fisher information and efficiencies (min sin^3 efficiency 0.9595 at alpha = 0.5 on a 501-point grid).

Populations thermal at each semimajor axis and total mass keep a uniform angle law under selection on true lengths, line-of-sight angles, semimajor axis and total mass that ignores sky position angles.
Binning by projected separation preserves the model when semimajor axes follow a log-uniform (Opik) law independent of shape, phase and orientation, and otherwise reweights by an explicit factor.
The inverse is discontinuous in total variation: eccentricity laws far apart in total variation can give angle laws arbitrarily close.
The inverse is continuous in the weak topology.
A grid maximum-likelihood fit recovers a step CDF with errors 0.103, 0.061, 0.036 at N = 2,000, 20,000, 100,000.

notClaimed: Any result about a real catalogue; all data are synthetic
Point identification of an individual binary's eccentricity
Novelty of angle-based eccentricity inference (Tokovinin 1998 onward)
Consistency or a rate for the grid fit; a proof of the observed 1/n decay; minimax rates; semiparametric efficiency
Historical priority beyond a bounded search
